physician_release_policy.combine: All conditions AND; missing, unknown, stale or contradictory evidence denies.
conditions: Authenticated active physician account, second factor satisfied, active nonexpired server session
Server-bound physician identity matches requested recipient; supplied role or organization cannot override it
Target patient has verified synthetic enrolment and unambiguous CNIC/order/specimen linkage
Requested report version is accepted or explicitly historical/superseded, not held; stored payload and issuer-bound provenance intact
Active explicit patient grant includes exact immutable version_id and matches physician, patient, appointment, hospital, affiliation and purpose
Server time >= starts_at and server time < expires_at
Appointment belongs to same patient and physician/context and is booked or confirmed, not cancelled or completed
Independent simulated professional registration is valid and within its evidence interval
Separate hospital affiliation is valid for that physician and hospital within its evidence interval
Required durable audit and protected-checkpoint status permits release
physician_release_policy.patient_read: Patient uses authenticated ownership plus accepted/intact report checks; physician credential/appointment/grant predicates are not applied to the patient's own record.
physician_release_policy.lab_read: Source laboratory staff use authenticated lab scope, order assignment and role; this does not create access to other labs or the patient's complete history.
physician_release_policy.deny_output: Never include result, filename, report count, CNIC, another patient's existence or unshared correction contents. Known own appointment may show a minimal actionable status; cross-owner and nonexistent object responses are indistinguishable.
physician_release_policy.historical_versions: A V1 grant can permit V1 after it is superseded if every other predicate still holds. A generic superseded warning can appear without revealing unshared V2 content or provenance. V2 always requires its own selected version grant.
physician_release_policy.no_blanket_permission: Hospital listing, affiliation, registration, appointment booking and account login each provide zero patient-record permission by themselves.

cybersecurity_design.identity: CNIC is an identity-matching attribute, never an authenticator, public username, authorization token or recovery secret. Normalize server-side; protect with encrypted storage and secret-keyed lookup; use opaque internal IDs and masked output.
cybersecurity_design.authentication: Proposed password hashing with a maintained library, separate local test second factor, rate limits, server-side sessions, logout invalidation, short inactivity and absolute expiry. No password/OTP secrets in browser bundle, URL or logs.
cybersecurity_design.browser_boundary: Session cookies HttpOnly, SameSite and Secure in the intended HTTPS setup; CSRF protection and origin checks for state changes. A documented isolated loopback-only development setup must not be represented as a production TLS deployment.
cybersecurity_design.transport_storage: TLS for any non-loopback access, encrypted sensitive store/backup, file storage outside public web root, restricted runtime account and separate fixture issuer/audit keys. No claim of protection from a fully compromised runtime/OS/key holder.
cybersecurity_design.issuer_integrity: Proposed per-lab asymmetric signing keys in local source simulators; ingest has trusted public keys only. A versioned canonical manifest binds issuer, source report/message IDs, patient mapping reference, order/specimen, exact content digest, version, predecessor, issue time and approver reference. Verify manifest signature AND actual file digest; a recomputed bare hash is insufficient.
cybersecurity_design.source_limits: A correctly signed report can still be clinically false. Source approval verifies synthetic origin/consistency, not collection truth or analytical validity. Key rotation retains historical verification evidence; compromise triggers explicit review/hold events rather than erasing provenance.
cybersecurity_design.submission_controls: Schema and field allowlists, exact allowed document types, bounded size/count, no active HTML rendering, safe text escaping, server-controlled paths, idempotency keys plus immutable source identity. Same key+same payload returns same receipt; same key+different payload conflicts.
cybersecurity_design.corrections: Unique report/version and one accepted successor per predecessor. Transaction checks expected head and distinct approver. A competing successor is held/conflicted, never silently wins. Original and evidence persist; never reassign accepted patient identity in place.
cybersecurity_design.current_state_release: One central authorization path covers lists, metadata and files. Browser visibility, role dropdowns, cached JWT claims, knowledge of IDs or a prior successful view cannot authorize a request.
cybersecurity_design.concurrency: Release decisions and relevant state changes use a single authoritative transaction/ordering mechanism with state revisions. An earlier in-flight authorized request may complete; requests ordered after committed withdrawal/cancellation/credential change must observe it. No claim to recall bytes already delivered.
cybersecurity_design.caching: Clinical HTTP responses private and no-store; no service-worker clinical cache or localStorage reports. File routes are independently gated, with no long-lived bearer download links. Clearing the display after denial does not erase external copies.
cybersecurity_design.audit: State-changing clinical/permission/credential operations and their audit events commit atomically in the primary durable store. Clinical release requires a durable decision event. Record delivery attempts/outcomes separately; no claim of proof of reading.
cybersecurity_design.tamper_evidence: Audit chain plus protected latest-head checkpoint outside the attacker-writable store detects the defined alteration/deletion/truncation tests. An unkeyed chain alone is insufficient. Protected key/checkpoint trust is an explicit assumption.
cybersecurity_design.audit_failure_recovery: Audit-write failure rolls back its coupled state change and blocks release. If advancing a protected checkpoint fails after primary commit, retain the committed state and enter recovery-required; release stays blocked. Verify against trusted recovery evidence/checkpoint before resuming; never silently re-anchor an untrusted store.
cybersecurity_design.minimization: Hospital has zero clinical access. Labs see own source work only. Physicians see granted exact versions only. Routine notifications contain only generic in-app status, no results/CNIC. Patient audit view is redacted and ownership-filtered.
cybersecurity_design.fail_closed: Unknown identity, missing credential evidence, stale status, invalid integrity, missing required audit or inconsistent recovery status prevents clinical release.
explicit_non_guarantees: No detection of every false but authorized clinical statement
No protection against a fully compromised OS plus protected keys
No evidence of stakeholder acceptance from synthetic demonstrations
cybersecurity_design.approval_binding: The authenticated distinct approver must match the issuer-bound source approval reference. Final approval rechecks the exact signed manifest and bytes; changing an approval or signed field requires a new valid package before acceptance.

proposed_indexes_and_transactions: Unique normalized keyed CNIC lookup for enrolled patients; no automatic duplicate-account merge.
Unique lab_id + source_report_id and lab_id + message_id; immutable receipt digest.
Unique report_id + version_number; at most one accepted successor for a predecessor; compare expected head.
Unique active physician/hospital/slot allocation with atomic conflict handling.
Grant version join table uses exact immutable version IDs; no wildcard/future versions.
Grant, appointment, credential and report status revisions are read with the release decision in the authoritative ordering transaction.
Clinical state mutation and audit append succeed or roll back together; protected checkpoint failure causes recovery hold.
All wall-clock comparisons use server/test clock; explicit inclusive start and exclusive end.
